hint.text: Commas are used to separate subordinate clauses from main clauses. There should be a comma placed after the subordinating clause, but only if it comes at the beginning of the sentence.

instruction.text: Select the subordinate clause in the sentence.

atoms.b: ((If you work hard,)) you will get good grades.
atoms.sound: If you work hard, you will get good grades.

instruction.text: Select the subordinate clause in the sentence.

atoms.b: Ella competed well ((even with a sore shoulder.))
atoms.sound: Ella competed well even with a sore shoulder.

instruction.text: Select the subordinate clause in the sentence.

atoms.b: ((As we had missed the bus,)) we had to walk to school.
atoms.sound: As we had missed the bus, we had to walk to school.

instruction.text: Select the subordinate clause in the sentence.

atoms.b: Mara’s phone had already run out of battery ((even though she’d charged it that morning)).
atoms.sound: Mara’s phone had already run out of battery even though she’d charged it that morning.

instruction.text: Drag the punctuation to correctly punctuate the subordinate clause.

atoms.a: As the sun is out today, make sure to put on some sun cream.
atoms.b: As the sun is out today((,)) make sure to put on some sun cream((.))

atoms.a: Jason walked extra quietly round the house because he did not want to disturb the baby.
atoms.b: Jason walked extra quietly round the house because he did not want to disturb the baby((. --,))

atoms.a: Even though she had always been a lawyer, Lara now fancied a career change.
atoms.b: Even though she had always been a lawyer((,)) Lara now fancied a career change((.))

atoms.a: As a result of the thick snow, all the local schools were closed.
atoms.b: As a result of the thick snow((,)) all the local schools were closed((.))
